parsed.title: Limiting increment conjecture for expected propagation times of n-Suns
parsed.statement:
For the $n\operatorname{-Sun}$ graph, let $\operatorname{ept}(n\operatorname{-Sun})$ denote its expected propagation time. **Limiting increment conjecture.**

$$
\lim_{n\rightarrow\infty} \left(\operatorname{ept}(n\operatorname{-Sun})-\operatorname{ept}((n-1)\operatorname{-Sun})\right)=\frac{11}{16}=0.6875.
$$

The conjecture is motivated by the tabulated numerical values of successive expected-propagation-time differences, which approach $0.6875$. Its status is not established in the supplied material.

parsed.title: Primality characterization for polyomino ideals without zig-zag walks
parsed.statement:
Let ${\mathcal P}$ be a polyomino. Its **polyomino ideal** $I_{\mathcal P}$ is the ideal associated with ${\mathcal P}$, and a **zig-zag walk** is a walk in ${\mathcal P}$ of the type described in the paper.

**Primality conjecture.** The following conditions are equivalent:

1. The polyomino ideal $I_{\mathcal P}$ is prime.
2. ${\mathcal P}$ contains no zig-zag walks.

This conjecture proposes a complete combinatorial characterization of the primality of polyomino ideals, extending the paper's results for polyominoes containing zig-zag walks, polyominoes of rank at most $14$, and grid polyominoes. Its resolution is not specified in the supplied text.

parsed.title: Farber's diameter conjecture for higher associahedra
parsed.statement:
Let $k$ and $n$ be positive integers with $n=2k$. For a bipartite $(k,2k)$-plabic graph $G$, let $G^{\operatorname{op}}$ be the graph obtained from $G$ by a $180^\circ$ rotation followed by changing the colors of all vertices. The **Farber diameter conjecture.** The diameter of the higher associahedron $\Upsigma_{\mathcal{A},k-1}$ equals

$$
\frac12 k(k-1)^2.
$$

More generally, the minimal number of square moves needed to connect $G$ with $G^{\operatorname{op}}$ equals

$$
\frac12 k(k-1)^2.
$$

This conjecture concerns the maximal square-move distance between regular plabic graphs and extends the corresponding diameter question for the ordinary associahedron. Its status is not resolved in the supplied source.

parsed.title: Strict log-concavity conjecture for the rank and crank of ordinary partitions
parsed.statement:
Let $N(m,n)$ and $M(m,n)$ denote, respectively, the rank and crank counting functions for ordinary partitions of $n$ with statistic $m$. **Strict log-concavity conjecture.** The following inequalities hold:

$$
N(m,n)^2 > N(m-1,n)N(m+1,n) \qquad\text{for } n\ge123 \text{ and } |m|\le n-72,
$$

$$
M(m,n)^2 > M(m-1,n)M(m+1,n) \qquad\text{for } n\ge125 \text{ and } |m|\le n-71.
$$

These are recorded as analogous conjectural strict log-concavity statements for the rank and crank of ordinary partitions; the supplied text gives no proof or resolution.

parsed.title: Descent distribution for pattern-avoiding 2-arrangements
parsed.statement:
Let $[n]=\{1,2,\ldots,n\}$, let a 2-arrangement of $[n-1]$ be represented in permutation form, and let $\mathop{\sf des}\nolimits$ denote the number of descents. **Descent-distribution conjecture.** For any one of the patterns $132$, $213$, $231$, or $312$, the distribution of the number of descents on 2-arrangements of $[n-1]$ whose permutation form avoids that pattern is given by triangle sequence A108838, with formula

$$
\frac{2}{n+1}\binom{n+1}{k+2}\binom{n-2}{k}.
$$

The sequence also counts, among other objects, rooted ordered trees with $n$ non-root nodes and $k$ leaves. The parser supplies no resolution evidence, so the conjecture remains open in this record.

parsed.title: Dvořák–Postle edge conjecture for $C_5$-critical graphs
parsed.statement:
For a graph $H$, an $H$-critical graph is a graph that admits no homomorphism to $H$, while every proper subgraph does. Here $C_5$ denotes the cycle on five vertices, and $e(G)=|E(G)|$, $v(G)=|V(G)|$.

**Dvořák–Postle conjecture.** If $G$ is $C_5$-critical, then

$$
e(G)\geq\frac{14v(G)-9}{11}.
$$

This conjecture concerns the density of graphs critical for homomorphisms to the five-cycle and is stated after a weaker proven bound in the source; no resolution is supplied here.

parsed.title: The \operatorname{SC}_{132} image conjecture for maximally nonperiodic permutations
parsed.statement:
Let $s_{132}$ be the classical stack-sorting map associated with the pattern $132$, let $\operatorname{Av}(132,231)$ denote the permutations avoiding $132$ and $231$, and define ${\bf V}_n$ by listing the odd elements of $[n]$ in decreasing order followed by the even elements in increasing order when $n$ is odd, with the analogous even-then-odd construction when $n$ is even.

**\operatorname{SC}_{132} image conjecture.** If $\tau\in S_n$ satisfies

$$
s_{132}^{n-2}(\tau)\notin\operatorname{Av}(132,231),
$$

then

$$
s_{132}^{n-1}(\tau)={\bf V}_n.
$$

The claim concerns permutations whose second-to-last iterate has not yet entered the known periodic-point set; the paper presents it as an additional open dynamical question.

parsed.title: Sankar's weighted tennis ball formula for the linear coefficient
parsed.statement:
Let $\operatorname{RedVHC}_k(\operatorname{Av}_{3k-i}(312))$ denote the set of $312$-avoiding reduced valid hook configurations with $k$ hooks on permutations with $2k+i$ points. Define

$$
f_k(x)=\sum_{i=0}^{k-1}\left|\operatorname{RedVHC}_k(\operatorname{Av}_{3k-i}(312))\right|x^i,
$$

and let $h_k(x)=f_k(x-1)$. **Sankar's conjecture.** The linear coefficient of $h_k(x)$ is given by the $(k-1)$st weighted tennis ball number. The supplied material does not define the weighted tennis ball numbers or give a resolution status for this conjecture.

parsed.title: Hypermodular matroid conjecture on same-rank modular extensions
parsed.statement:
We assume all matroids are finite. A matroid is **modular** if every pair of its flats is modular, and **hypermodular** if every pair of its maximal proper flats is modular. A matroid is a **restriction** of another matroid when it is obtained by restricting that matroid to a subset of its ground set.

**Hypermodular matroid conjecture.** Every hypermodular matroid is a restriction of a modular matroid of the same rank.

This is a 2011 rephrasing of the modular-extension problem for hypermodular matroids. The supplied source does not state whether the conjecture has been resolved.

parsed.title: The iterated-blow-up conjecture for $\{K_4^{3-},C_5\}$
parsed.statement:
Let $G$ be the iterated blow-up of an edge, obtained from a complete balanced $3$-partite $3$-graph by inserting a complete balanced $3$-partite $3$-graph recursively in each part. This $3$-graph is $\{K_4^{3-},C_5\}$-free and gives the lower bound $\sigma(\{K_4^{3-},C_5\})\geq 1/13$. **The iterated-blow-up conjecture for $\{K_4^{3-},C_5\}$.** The graph $G$ is the extremal example in $\ell_2$-norm; in particular,

$$
\sigma(\{K_4^{3-},C_5\})=\frac{1}{13}.
$$

The construction is described as the current best lower-bound example, and no matching upper bound or resolution is supplied.

parsed.title: The codegree-squared density conjecture for $K_5^4$
parsed.statement:
Let $K_5^4$ be the $4$-uniform hypergraph on five vertices with five edges. The matrix construction described in the text gives

$$
\frac{31}{64}\leq\sigma(K_5^4)\leq 0.55241250.
$$

**The codegree-squared density conjecture for $K_5^4$.** The lower bound is tight:

$$
\sigma(K_5^4)=\frac{31}{64}.
$$

The lower bound comes from the construction and the upper bound from flag algebras; the supplied text does not resolve whether equality holds.

parsed.title: Grünbaum's catalogue conjecture for simplicial line arrangements
parsed.statement: A **simplicial line arrangement** is a finite arrangement of lines in $\mathbb{P}^{2}_{\mathbb{R}}$ whose complement has only open triangular connected components. Grünbaum's catalogue consists of three infinite families together with approximately $90$ sporadic examples. **Grünbaum's catalogue conjecture.** Except for finitely many corrections, Grünbaum's catalogue is complete. Equivalently, one expects that there are only three infinite families of simplicial line arrangements. The paper studies this classification problem and provides a complete classification of nearly free, non-free simplicial arrangements with at most $27$ lines; the source gives no resolution of the catalogue conjecture itself.

parsed.title: Cuntz–Geis bound for sporadic simplicial line arrangements
parsed.statement:
Let $\mathcal{L}$ be a **sporadic simplicial line arrangement** in $\mathbb{P}^{2}_{\mathbb{R}}$, meaning a simplicial line arrangement outside the known infinite families, and let $d$ be its number of lines. **Cuntz–Geis conjecture.** Then

$$
d\leqslant 37.
$$

This is a stronger conjecture related to Grünbaum's catalogue conjecture, predicting a uniform upper bound on the number of lines in a sporadic simplicial arrangement. The source does not state a resolution.

parsed.title: The Polynexus formula for nonzero products in the rook monoid
parsed.statement:
Let $M_n$ be the monoid of rook diagrams and let $\mathbf{0}$ denote its zero element. Let $\psi(n)$ be the number of nonzero products arising from $M_n\setminus\{\mathbf{0}\}$.

**Polynexus conjecture.** For $n\in\mathbb{N}$, $\psi(n)$ equals the $(n+1)$th Polynexus number of order $7$, namely

$$
\psi(n)=\frac{(n+1)^7-n^7-(n+1)^3+n^3}{120}.
$$

The formula was suggested by numerical evaluation of the sextuple sum defining $\psi(n)$ and comparison with the Polynexus numbers. An analytic evaluation of that sum was not available in the source, so the conjecture remains open here.

parsed.title: Chen et al.'s refined BFP conjecture for near-complete bipartite graphs
parsed.statement:
Let $p,q,e$ be positive integers with $p\leq q$ and $pq-p<e<pq$. Let $K_{p,q}$ be the complete bipartite graph with partite-set orders $p$ and $q$, and let $\mathcal{K}(p,q,e)$ be the family of its subgraphs with precisely $e$ edges, no isolated vertices, and which are not complete bipartite graphs. For a graph $G$, let $\rho(G)$ denote its spectral radius. For $e>pq-p$, let $K^e_{p,q}$ denote the graph obtained from $K_{p,q}$ by deleting $pq-e$ edges incident on a common vertex in the partite set of order $q$. **Chen et al.'s refined BFP conjecture.** An extremal graph attaining

$$
\max_{G\in\mathcal{K}(p,q,e)}\rho(G)
$$

is obtained by $K^e_{p,q}$. This refinement concerns the high-edge regime of the BFP problem and was proved by Liu and Weng in 2015.
parsed.source_name: Yen-Jen Cheng, Chia-An Liu and Chih-wen Weng, “Counterexamples of the Bhattacharya-Friedland-Peled conjecture”, arXiv:2112.01124 (2021).
parsed.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2112.01124

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of December 2021). “This conjecture was proved in 1988 by Rowlinson .”

Let $G$) be a path graph with $n$ vertices, and for $1\leq h\leq \left\lfloor n/2\right\rfloor$ let $\zeta^{(h)}=12\cdots(n-h)n(n-1)\cdots(n-h+1)$. For a permutation $\pi=\pi_1\cdots\pi_n\in S_n$, write

\operatorname{TPro}_\pi=\tau_{\pi_n}\tau_{\pi_{n-1}}\cdots\tau_{\pi_1}\colon\Lambda_G\to\Lambda_G.
$$

parsed.title: Coxeter polynomial conjecture for non-negative posets of Dynkin type
parsed.statement:
Let $I$ be a poset with at most $13$ elements, and let $\mathrm{cox}_I(t)$ denote its Coxeter polynomial. Write $\mathrm{Dyn}_I$ for its Dynkin type, and call $I$ **non-negative** when its associated quadratic form is non-negative. A poset is **connected** when its Hasse diagram is connected. 

**Coxeter polynomial conjecture.** If

$$
\mathrm{cox}_I(t)=t^n+t^{n-1}+\cdots+t+1,
$$

then $I$ is connected. If, additionally, $I$ is non-negative, then

$$
\mathrm{Dyn}_I=\mathbb{A}_{|I|}.
$$

The conjecture proposes that, for posets of at most $13$ elements, this cyclotomic Coxeter polynomial forces connectedness, and in the non-negative case identifies the Dynkin type as $\mathbb{A}_{|I|}$. It follows an example showing that the Coxeter polynomial alone does not preserve positivity of posets.
parsed.source_name: M. Gąsiorek, “A Coxeter type classification of Dynkin type A_n non-negative posets”, arXiv:2205.15813 (2023).
parsed.references:
**2 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2021–2022). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:2112.15587](https://arxiv.org/abs/2112.15587).
